name: baldurs_gate
lore:
### **Baldur’s Gate: The Jewel of the Sword Coast**

**Overview**
Perched precariously at the mouth of the River Chionthar, Baldur’s Gate stands as a titan of stone, iron, and fog. It is a sovereign city-state, a melting pot of ambition, and arguably the most influential mercantile hub on the Sword Coast. 

**History**
The city began as "Gray Harbor," a haven for smugglers and pirates. Its transformation began with the legendary explorer **Balduran**, who returned from the fabled West laden with unimaginable wealth. He funded the construction of the Great Wall, providing the security necessary for the settlement to evolve from a muddy port into a sprawling metropolis. Over centuries, the city expanded beyond its walls, surviving sieges, plagues, and the internal strife of its ruling "Patriars."

**Significance**
Baldur’s Gate is the beating heart of trade between the frozen North and the glittering South. It is divided into three districts: the opulent **Upper City**, the bustling **Lower City**, and the lawless **Outer City**. Order is maintained—often brutally—by the **Flaming Fist**, a mercenary company turned city watch. For an adventurer, the Gate is a place where a pauper can become a duke, provided they have the steel to survive the shadows.

**Legends and Lore**
No city is so haunted by the divine. Baldur’s Gate was the epicenter of the **Bhaalspawn Crisis**, where the mortal children of the God of Murder vied for his empty throne. More recently, the city narrowly escaped the "Descent," a hellish plot that saw its neighbor, Elturel, dragged into Avernus. Whispers persist that Balduran himself never truly died, but remains bound to the city’s foundations, waiting for its darkest hour to return.

*“In the Gate, coin is king, but iron is the law.” — Common Adage*

subLocations.name: elfsong tavern
subLocations.lore:
History
The tavern circa 1374 DR.
The tavern circa 1374 DR.

The Elfsong Tavern was one of the city's most popular taverns in the mid-1300s DR.[2]

In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, when the Dark Alliance first began to threaten Baldur's Gate, the Elfsong Tavern was where the fight began. Vahn, Kromlech, and Adrianna were attacked by thieves working for the Dark Alliance and recovered in the Elfsong Tavern. From the Elfsong Tavern they eventually went to the Onyx Tower, where they learned the secrets of the Elfsong. The ghostly elven woman who sang in the tavern sang for her husband, who had worked for the Company of the Crescent Blade. Her husband had left to defend Baldur's Gate and promised one day to return but never did. She continued to sing because she was still waiting for him to come home. In the Onyx Tower, the three adventurers met a ghost who revealed himself to be the husband of the elf woman. The destruction of the Onyx Tower freed the ghost and brought the elf woman peace.[3]

During the Absolute Crisis in the Year of Three Ships Sailing, 1492 DR, Duke Belynne Stelmane was murdered by Bhaalists in the Elfsong Tavern. Her hand was severed and her body staged to appear as part of a plan by the Cult of the Absolute to sow fear in the city.

subLocations.name: sorcerous sundries
subLocations.lore:
History
While Sorcerous Sundries was established as a store for the arcane, for many years the building was used as a private residence, a restaurant, a variety of specialty shops, and even a greenhouse.[2]

Sometime during the 15th century DR, Rivalen Blackhand re-founded the store as a shop catering to spellcasters, specializing in Material components. However, he denied having magic items for sale and outright refused to sell spell scrolls.

subLocations.name: The Wide
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Upper City]] of [[Baldur's Gate]] that served as a vast open-air marketplace and plaza.

subLocations.name: Citadel Streets
subLocations.lore: A small and rather segregated district located on the north side of the [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Manorborn
subLocations.lore: One of the four districts that composed the [[Upper City]], home to the richest members of the Baldurian [[patriar]], nearly every member of the [[Parliament of Peers]] resided in the district.

subLocations.name: Temples District
subLocations.lore: The largest and perhaps the oldest and most important region in the entirety of the [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Seatower
subLocations.lore: One of the largest districts of [[Baldur's Gate]], located on the northern shore of the [[River Chionthar]] and housed the western docks of [[Gray Harbor]].

subLocations.name: Bloomridge
subLocations.lore: A wealthy district within the [[Lower City]], south of the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]], into which it was partially built via great feats of engineering, both structural and [[arcane]].

subLocations.name: The Steeps
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Lower City]] between the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]] and the eastern side of [[Gray Harbor]].

subLocations.name: Heapside
subLocations.lore: A large district in the [[Lower City]], that gained its name following the [[Tax Revolts]] of the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Eastway
subLocations.lore: One of the larger districts of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Brampton
subLocations.lore: A district in south-eastern Baldur's Gate, noteworthy in that passage through it, was required to reach the [[Outer City]] district of [[Tumbledown]].

subLocations.name: Blackgate
subLocations.lore: The region that served as a waiting area for merchants and caravaneers moving their goods along the [[Trade Way]]. They were forced to stable their pack animals in Blackgate, while their products were transferred to another conveyance while moving through the city.

subLocations.name: Stonyeyes
subLocations.lore: The neighborhood that was home to a large community of [[half-orc]]s, many of whom worked as porters, helped in transporting goods to and from caravans coming to [[Baldur's Gate]], as their pack animals were not allowed within the city walls.

subLocations.name: Little Calimshan
subLocations.lore: A rowdy and chaotic walled district in the [[Outer City]], distinct in its design and atmosphere that evoked its namesake realm of [[Calimshan]].

subLocations.name: Norchapel
subLocations.lore: An [[Outer City]] neighborhood, home to many laborers and criminal gangs.

subLocations.name: Whitkeep
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Outer City]],  home to a sizable community of [[gnome]]s, many of whom worked as [[tin]]smiths within the city.

subLocations.name: Sow's Foot
subLocations.lore: A district in the [[Outer City]] – the easternmost neighborhood located outside of the city walls, nestled in between [[Twin Songs]] and [[Whitkeep]].

subLocations.name: Twin Songs
subLocations.lore: A district of the [[Outer City]] located on the northern side of the [[Wyrm's Crossing]] bridge that was an expansive collection of temples and shrines dedicated to nearly every deity including dark and malevolent deities.

subLocations.name: Tumbledown
subLocations.lore: A lone and perpetually foggy district located within the [[Outer City]], the location of the [[Cliffside Cemetery]].

subLocations.name: Rivington
subLocations.lore: The southernmost district of [[Baldur's Gate]] and the only region of the [[Outer City]] located on the southern shore of the [[River Chionthar]].

subLocations.name: Wyrm's Crossing
subLocations.lore: This district was comprised of two massively-tall stone bridges that spanned the length of the [[River Chionthar]].

subLocations.name: Water Queen's House
subLocations.lore: A temple dedicated to [[Umberlee]], the Bitch Queen – the city's oldest temple.

subLocations.name: High House of Wonders
subLocations.lore: A grand temple to [[Gond]] Wondermaker that consisted of numerous expansive workshops within which the [[Gondar]] [[priest]]s created experimental devices and machinations for the Baldurian people.

subLocations.name: Lady's Hall
subLocations.lore: A prosperous temple of [[Tymora]], the Lady Luck, built soon after the founding of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Watchful Shield
subLocations.lore: A shrine of [[Helm]] the Vigilant, located in the [[Manorborn]] district of [[Baldur's Gate]] within a diminutive chapel with wings extending from either side of its front doorway, and the [[silver]] eye of Helm inscribed above.

subLocations.name: Shrine of the Suffering
subLocations.lore: A shrine of [[Ilmater]], the Maimed God, established before [[1358 DR]] that served as a soup kitchen in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Sewer Keep
subLocations.lore: The tower complex used as a magic water treatment facility that purified sewage waste before it is washed into the [[River Chionthar]].

subLocations.name: Seatower of Balduran
subLocations.lore: The massive sea-fortress that rested on a rocky island in the city's bay that served as the headquarters of the [[Flaming Fist]] in the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: High Hall
subLocations.lore: Also known as the '''Ducal Palace'', the seat of the [[Council of Four]] in which city business was conducted.

subLocations.name: Watch Citadel
subLocations.lore: Also known as '''Stormkeep''', the headquarters of [[the Watch]] in [[Baldur's Gate]] that served as a staging area, training grounds, and a temporary holding area, when needed.

subLocations.name: Hissing Stones
subLocations.lore: A bathhouse and a local landmark with a sterling reputation as the city's safest and most confidential meeting area among the various Baldurian power groups.

subLocations.name: Fury of the Fist
subLocations.lore: A statue located outside the [[Seatower of Balduran]], west of the drawbridge, vandalized by [[thieves]] in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: Mandorcai's Mansion
subLocations.lore: A mysterious manor in the [[Bloomridge]] neighborhood, believed to have been built by its namesake – [[tiefling]] [[wizard]] [[Mandorcai]], in reality, its origin was much more [[fiend]]ish in nature.

subLocations.name: Seskergates
subLocations.lore: A tower of a manse of the [[Sesker]] mercantile clan, purchased by the eccentric Baldurian court-[[mage]] named [[Imbralym Skoond]] in the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: The Smilin' Boar
subLocations.lore: One of Bloomridge's most trendy eateries, serving bawdier versions of traditional morningfeast dishes such as "[[sow's delight]]" and "[[three pigs in a blanket]]", and [[coffee]] and [[tea]] was served in mugs that were shaped like a [[pig]]'s head.

subLocations.name: Citadel Gate
subLocations.lore: The city gate that separated [[Watch Citadel]] and its surrounding district from the rest of the [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Gond Gate
subLocations.lore: One of the city's landmark "[[patriar]] gates."

subLocations.name: Manor Gate
subLocations.lore: A landmark gate in the old wall that separated the [[Upper City]] district of [[Manorborn]] from the [[Lower City]] district of [[Bloomridge]].

subLocations.name: Sea Gate
subLocations.lore: A landmark and one of the city's four, generally lesser well-known, "[[patriar]] gates" that connected the poor [[Lower City]] to the [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Baldur's Gate
subLocations.lore: One of the oldest landmarks and the eponymous city gate that gave the famed port metropolis of the [[Sword Coast]] its name.

subLocations.name: Heap Gate
subLocations.lore: One of the city's four, smaller "[[patriar]] gates" that connected the poorer [[Lower City]] to the affluent [[Upper City]].

subLocations.name: Black Dragon Gate
subLocations.lore: Also known as the '''Landward Gate''', the grand northward gate that allowed a passageway through the northern wall of [[Baldur's Gate]], decorated with a large stone sculpture of a [[black dragon]] head that loomed over the inner side of the wall.

subLocations.name: Basilisk Gate
subLocations.lore: The landmark gate lined with statues of prominent deceased [[patriar]], including one of [[Entar Silvershield]] placed above the gate in the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Cliffgate
subLocations.lore: A landmark gate that served as a passageway connecting the [[Lower City]] to the isolated district of [[Tumbledown]] in the [[Outer City]].

subLocations.name: Bormul House
subLocations.lore: The elegant three-story townhouse of yellow [[granite]], home to the Baldurian branch of the [[Amn]]ian [[Bormul Dynasty]].

subLocations.name: Hhune House
subLocations.lore: The palatial manse home of the influential [[patriar]] [[Hhune]] family, relatives of the royal house of [[Tethyr]].

subLocations.name: Eomane House
subLocations.lore: The estate home of the [[Eomane]] family that controlled the most elite [[perfume]]ry in the city as well as [[fish]] and lamp [[fish oil]] processing factories.

subLocations.name: Rillyn House
subLocations.lore: The house of the [[Rillyn]] [[patriar]] family of '''[[Baldur's Gate]]''', built on wealth gained through adventuring.

subLocations.name: Vanthampur Villa
subLocations.lore: Home to the wealthy [[patriar]] noble [[Vanthampur]] family in [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Helm and Cloak
subLocations.lore: A high-end inn, rooming house, and [[festhall]], popular both with travelers and with local residents, who enjoyed its resplendent dining room. It was also home to the majority of the [[Knights of the Unicorn]], who rented most of the upper floor.

subLocations.name: Unrolling Scroll
subLocations.lore: A white [[marble]] building with a red roof and [[gold]] leaf trim – a shrine to [[Oghma]], the Patron of all Bards.

subLocations.name: Hall of Wonders
subLocations.lore: A museum in [[Baldur's Gate]] that displayed both the pragmatic and fantastical "holy relics" of the [[Church of Gond]].

subLocations.name: Ramazith's Tower
subLocations.lore: The landmark tower built by renowned [[sage]] and zoologist, [[Ramazith Flamesinger]], sometime before [[1368 DR]]; it was purchased by the [[Athkatlan]] [[mage]] [[Lorroakan]] in  [[1492 DR]].

subLocations.name: Three Old Kegs
subLocations.lore: A well-known inn widely regarded as one of the best establishments in all of [[Faerûn]], and was known for its comfortable furnishings and generally somnific atmosphere.

subLocations.name: Distant Shores
subLocations.lore: A merchant of imported goods and products native to [[Chult]].

subLocations.name: Harbreeze Bakery
subLocations.lore: A bakery offered such favorite delicacies as [[cinnamon]] [[cookie]]s and full loaves of [[sugarbread]] highlighted by the flavors of foreign [[tea]]s and [[spice]]s.

subLocations.name: Felogyr's Fireworks
subLocations.lore: A four-story stone shop on [[Bindle Street]] that traded in [[fireworks]], [[torch]]es, [[candle]] wicks, and other lesser alchemical items, and as of the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]], the sole producer of [[smokepowder]] within [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Beloved Ranger
subLocations.lore: A large statue that portrayed a larger-than-life depiction of the [[Rashemaar]] [[ranger]] [[Minsc]] and his rodent companion, both were revealed to be [[petrified]] heroes, released in the 1480s [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Blushing Mermaid
subLocations.lore: A famous lower-class tavern that provided drinks and food and was known for its shady associations, rumors of secret smuggling passages, and hidden vaults underneath.

subLocations.name: Baldur's Mouth
subLocations.lore: A narrow, five-story printshop that disseminated news via [[broadsheet]]s and town criers.

subLocations.name: Counting House
subLocations.lore: The center of trade and business in [[Baldur's Gate]], serving as both a bank and establishment that facilitated the exchange of various currencies.

subLocations.name: Sorcerous Sundries
subLocations.lore: A magic shop on [[Stormshore Street]] in the [[Heapside]] district.

subLocations.name: Elfsong Tavern
subLocations.lore: A well-known tavern famed for its singing [[ghost]], [[Elfsong Cider|cider]], and a stuffed baby [[beholder]].

subLocations.name: Low Lantern
subLocations.lore: A three-mast ship converted to be used as a [[festhall]], tavern, and gambling house.

subLocations.name: Eastway Expeditions
subLocations.lore: A shop that specialized in selling equipment to those who sought exploration or adventure, particularly those ''en route'' to the [[Chultan Peninsula]].

subLocations.name: Blade and Stars
subLocations.lore: A quiet inn known for its high-quality foodstuffs, and a legend of a [[yuan-ti]] being trapped within the inn's walls, imprisoned while fighting a [[wizard]].

subLocations.name: Candulhallow's Funeral Arrangements
subLocations.lore: A city-sponsored business that specialized in the transportation and occasionally sale of corpses to cemeteries or temples.

subLocations.name: Jopalin's
subLocations.lore: Once a seedy tavern serving sailors, turned into a [[tea]] and [[coffee]]-sipping cafe after such establishments became popular in the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Garmult's House of Mastery
subLocations.lore: An academy that specialized in tutoring pupils on how to improve their martial prowess and combat skills and a social club for the members of the [[Bannerless Legion]] crew.

subLocations.name: Harborside Hospital
subLocations.lore: Formerly [[Scarbradro's Haven]], a hospital within the [[Brampton]] district with its [[cleric]]al staff offering medical services to anyone regardless of faith. Quality of service varied depending on the patient's wealth.

subLocations.name: Insight Park
subLocations.lore: A public park that was magically created during the mid–15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Danthelon's Dancing Axe
subLocations.lore: A general store that sold good quality secondhand wares, from pots and pans to [[rope]], [[armor]], and [[weapons]].

subLocations.name: Wyrm's Rock
subLocations.lore: A [[granite]] fortress that loomed over the small islet that connected the bridges of [[Wyrm's Crossing]].

subLocations.name: Church of Last Hope
subLocations.lore: A sanctuary not dedicated to any particular faith that offered shelter to the despondent, depressed, and hopeless wretches of the city and beyond.

subLocations.name: Hamhocks Slaughterhouse
subLocations.lore: A massive compound composed of a number of animal pens, knackeries, and butcheries, its foul stench drove away the animals of the herders and wranglers.

subLocations.name: Whitkeep Hostel
subLocations.lore: A large manor that served a number of purposes throughout its existence; during the later 15{{th}} century [[DR]], a [[gnome|gnomish]] artists' commune resided within.

subLocations.name: Garynmor Stables and Menagerie
subLocations.lore: A business that specialized in the handling and care of mundane beasts of burden, as well as the exhibition of all manner of exotic and fantastical creatures.

subLocations.name: The Oasis
subLocations.lore: A theater known for the rich production values of its show and the lavish spectacles it was capable of exhibiting in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Balduran Looks Out to Sea
subLocations.lore: A statue that depicted the famous explorer [[Balduran]], after whom the city was named.

subLocations.name: Cliffside Cemetery
subLocations.lore: The largest graveyard in [[Baldur's Gate]], a sprawling plot of land turned cemetery around the  [[Szarr]] family tombs and the [[Szarr Mansion]].

subLocations.name: Dusthawk Hill
subLocations.lore: A tall, yellow [[granite]] steep-faced hill east of the city walls.

subLocations.name: River Chionthar
subLocations.lore: A large river that ran through the [[Western Heartlands]].

subLocations.name: Riverveins
subLocations.lore: A collection of subterranean mostly submerged tunnels that mazed and drained into subterranean aquifers.

subLocations.name: Sailor's Crossing
subLocations.lore: A pier-side cobblestone plaza with a fountain at its center and the site of a grizzly murder in [[1477 DR]].

subLocations.name: Admiral's Way
subLocations.lore: A dockside [[salt]]-strewn street with the [[Low Lantern]] located at its eastern end.

subLocations.name: Fisher's Wharf
subLocations.lore: A pier used by fishing vessels and an occasional live-in boat roped to the docks.

subLocations.name: Silver Crescent Beach
subLocations.lore: A southwestern beach in the city and the location of a washed ashore corpse – part of a series of grizzly murders, in [[1477 DR]].

subLocations.name: Loklee Street
subLocations.lore: The street that owed its name to the small fishing village that eventually grew to be known as [[Baldur's Gate]]; it crossed with [[Stormshore Street]] in the north.

subLocations.name: Trade Way
subLocations.lore: An ancient, long, well-traveled trade road along the west coast of [[Faerûn]].

subLocations.name: Coast Way
subLocations.lore: A long, well-traveled part of the much larger [[Trade Way]] that started at [[Calimport]] in the south and went along the coastline all the way north to [[Waterdeep]].

subLocations.name: Silvershield Estate
subLocations.lore: The family home of the [[Silvershield]] [[patriar]] family of [[Baldur's Gate]] – a massive grand complex nearly the size of an entire city block that offered little comfort and coziness to its inhabitants and visitors.

subLocations.name: Old Wall
subLocations.lore: The wall that encircled the affluent [[Upper City]] of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Harbormaster's Office
subLocations.lore: The main civic building in the harbours of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Stormshore Street
subLocations.lore: A street that began in the northernmost top of the harbors, circled the [[Heapside]], passed [[Sorcerous Sundries]], hooked back west, and ended at the [[Stormshore Street Dock]] where the [[Low Lantern]] was [[anchor]]ed.

subLocations.name: Stormshore Street
subLocations.lore: A street that began in the northernmost top of the harbors, circled the [[Heapside]], passed [[Sorcerous Sundries]], hooked back west, and ended at the [[Stormshore Street Dock]] where the [[Low Lantern]] was [[anchor]]ed.

subLocations.name: Stormshore Street
subLocations.lore: A street that began in the northernmost top of the harbors, crossed [[Loklee Street]], circled the [[Heapside]], passed [[Sorcerous Sundries]], hooked back west, and ended at the [[Stormshore Street Dock]] where the [[Low Lantern]] was [[anchor]]ed.

subLocations.name: Stormshore Street Dock
subLocations.lore: Docks at the southern end of [[Stormshore Street]].

subLocations.name: Bindle Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]] by [[Felogyr's Fireworks]], ran south with a slight curve, passed the [[Blushing Mermaid]], crossed [[Stormshore Street]], and, eventually, ended at a dock near [[Fisher's Wharf]].

subLocations.name: Gray Harbor
subLocations.lore: The harbor of [[Baldur's Gate]] on [[River Chionthar]], one of the busiest and deepest natural harbors in [[Faerûn]].

subLocations.name: Calim Jewel Emporium
subLocations.lore: Shop and home to the most well-regarded [[Baldurian]] jeweler of the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]] and a forum for local agents of the criminal organization known as [[the Guild]].

subLocations.name: Splurging Sturgeon
subLocations.lore: Once a threadbare inn and tavern, turned into a fanciful eatery specializing in seafood, both exotic and local in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: Purple Wyrm Inn and Tavern
subLocations.lore: A very famous inn and tavern frequented by merchants, business owners, and adventurers.

subLocations.name: Omduil's Manor
subLocations.lore: Home to [[Omduil]], sage and seer for hire in the 14{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Rose Portal
subLocations.lore: A stone building with rose-colored windows that held the shrine dedicated to [[Lathander]] that somewhat falled out of favour by the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Seaserpent Tamed by Umberlee
subLocations.lore: A statue dedicated to [[Umberlee]], the Bitch Queen, that rose out of the [[Gray Harbor]] waters.

subLocations.name: Six Wise Machinists
subLocations.lore: A statue that was vandalized in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: Faithful Shopkeeper Meets the Honest Trader
subLocations.lore: A statue vandalized by thieves in [[1482 DR]].

subLocations.name: Undercellar's Main Entrance
subLocations.lore: A clump of chambers in a network of storage cellars beneath [[Baldur's Gate]] that housed a sleazy tavern and [[festhall]]; there existed at least twenty-four ways in and out of this popular establishment, half of which connected to other buildings.

subLocations.name: The Queen's Favor
subLocations.lore: A statue landmark of note.

subLocations.name: Jhasso Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Jhasso]] [[patria]]r family of [[Baldur's Gate]], part-owners of the [[Seven Suns Trading Coster]].

subLocations.name: Ulvur's Lane
subLocations.lore: A short lane that rang along the southern side of the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]] from two city blocks west of the [[Gond Gate]].

subLocations.name: House of the Lute
subLocations.lore: A modest [[kaeth]] house and [[minstrel]]s' gallery that offered classes from master musicians to its customers.

subLocations.name: Hammaskarl's Ride
subLocations.lore: The street that began at the [[Basilisk Gate]], curved south, then moved west past [[Eastway Expeditions]], and ended on an interception with [[Loklee Street]].

subLocations.name: Talankar's Lane
subLocations.lore: The street that began at the [[Basilisk Gate]] and ran northwest, passing the [[Blade and Stars]], the [[Elfsong Tavern]], and ended at the [[Heap Gate]].

subLocations.name: Ascloakan's Fine Inn
subLocations.lore: An inn of note at the meeting of [[Hammaskarl's Ride]] and [[Talankar's Lane]].

subLocations.name: The Fool's Altar
subLocations.lore: A shrine dedicated to [[Finder Wyvernspur]], the Nameless Bard, next-door to [[Ascloakan's Fine Inn]]; the shrine was supervised by the [[saurial]] [[priest]] named [[Aszloakh the Hooded]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Coran's Manor
subLocations.lore: Home to the wealthy adventurer-turned-politician named [[Coran]], until his death in [[1492 DR]].

subLocations.name: Candlekeep Chandlery
subLocations.lore: A shop that sold beautifying products and [[candle]]s, both mundane and magical in nature.

subLocations.name: Hullhollyn Estate
subLocations.lore: The family manse of a prominent [[patriar]] family – House [[Hullhollyn]], that ran a sizable merchant fleet.

subLocations.name: Sashenstar Estate
subLocations.lore: The home to the wealthy [[Sashenstar]] [[patriar]] family, members of the [[Merchant's League]], who owned shipping, mining, and textile operations.

subLocations.name: Shattershield Estate
subLocations.lore: The home to the only non-[[human]] [[patriar]] family – [[Shattershield]], that was instrumental in building the city's [[Old Walls (Baldur's Gate)|Old Walls]].

subLocations.name: Vannath Estate
subLocations.lore: The manse that belongs to the [[Vannath]] [[patriar]] family that fled to [[Baldur's Gate]] from [[Neverwinter]] after the [[Spellplague]].

subLocations.name: Oberon Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Oberon (family)|Oberon]] [[patriar]] family of [[Baldur's Gate]] that owned the majority of the city's dry docks.

subLocations.name: Belt Estate
subLocations.lore: The manse of the [[Belt (family)|Belt]] [[patriar]] family that built its wealth via the business holdings related to the sale and exchange of horses.

subLocations.name: Eltan Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Eltan]] [[patriar]] family that was connected to the founding of the [[Flaming Fist]].

subLocations.name: Ravenshade Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Ravenshade]] [[patriar]] family that dealt in [[ink]]s, [[dye]]s, [[gem]]s, and jewelry.

subLocations.name: Durinbold Estate
subLocations.lore: The estate of the [[Durinbold]] [[patriar]] family that owned numerous [[sheep]] herds and was related to the nobility of [[Waterdeep]].

subLocations.name: Caldwell Estate
subLocations.lore: Home of the [[Caldwell]] clan – one of the oldest and richest [[patriar]] families of [[Baldur's Gate]].

subLocations.name: Gist Estate
subLocations.lore: The estate of the [[Gist]] [[patriar]] family.

subLocations.name: Vammas Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Vammas]] [[patriar]] family.

subLocations.name: Redlocks Estate
subLocations.lore: The [[Redlocks]] [[patriar]] family manse, the clan that was rumored to have had an affiliation with piracy.

subLocations.name: Nurthammas Estate
subLocations.lore: The Estate of the [[Nurthammas]] [[patriar]] family that dealt in supplying ships for long voyages.

subLocations.name: Whitburn Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Whitburn]] [[patriar]] family that owned a [[slate]] quarry.

subLocations.name: Provoss Estate
subLocations.lore: The estate of the [[Provoss]] [[patriar]] family that faced hardships after dire cattle herd losses in the 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Portyr Estate
subLocations.lore: The estate of a ruling Ducal [[Portyr]] family of [[Baldur's Gate]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Stelmane Estate
subLocations.lore: The estate of a ruling Ducal [[Stelmane]] family of [[Baldur's Gate]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Linnacker Estate
subLocations.lore: The home manse of the [[Linnacker]]  [[patriar]] that made wealth from [[gem]] mines in [[Tethyr]].

subLocations.name: Jannath Estate
subLocations.lore: The estate of the [[Jannath]] [[patriar]] family that owned profitable [[copper]] mines.

subLocations.name: Miyar Estate
subLocations.lore: Home to a family member of the [[Merchant’s League]] – the [[Miyar]] [[patriar]] family that controlled the caravan supply and repair businesses.

subLocations.name: Oathoon Estate
subLocations.lore: The manse of the [[Oathoon]] [[patriar]] family that traded in [[wine]]s and spirits.

subLocations.name: Hlath Estate
subLocations.lore: The home estate of the influential [[Hlath (family)|Hlath]] [[patriar]] family.

subLocations.name: Tillerturn Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Tillerturn]] [[patria]]r family of [[Baldur's Gate]] that owned the lion's share of the city's buildings.

subLocations.name: Dlusker Estate
subLocations.lore: The home of the [[Dlusker]] textile [[patriar]] family, down on its luck in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Guthmere Estate
subLocations.lore: The family estate of the [[Guthmere]] [[patriar]] family that owned many butcheries and tanneries.

subLocations.name: Manycoins House
subLocations.lore: The office of the [[Merchant's League]] – a four-storied temple dedicated to [[Waukeen]] that offered mercantile services, short-term lodgings, and priestly services.

subLocations.name: Home of Krammoch Arkhstaff
subLocations.lore: The office and home of [[sage]] and retired adventurer Krammoch Arkhstaff in the late 14{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Home of Ragefast
subLocations.lore: The office and home of the well-respected sage named [[Ragefast]] in the late 14th century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Windspell Street
subLocations.lore: The street that stretched from the [[Citadel Gate]], passed [[Helm and Cloak]],  and separated the [[High House of Wonders]] from the [[Hall of Wonders]].

subLocations.name: Belltoll Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at [[The Wide]] by the [[Hlath (family)|Hlath Estate]], moved southwest past the [[High Hall]] and the [[Helm and Cloak]] inn, and ended soon after after crossing [[Sornbanner Street]].

subLocations.name: Wendserpent Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at [[Black Eel Street]], moved north through the [[Manor Gate]], crossed [[Belltoll Street]], then [[Windspell Street]], passed in front of the [[Black Dragon Gate]], curved along the city walls, passed [[Rose Portal]] shrine, and curved to [[the Wide]], where it ended.

subLocations.name: The Run
subLocations.lore: Thr road that stretched from the [[Watch Citadel]] to the [[Black Dragon Gate]].

subLocations.name: Canary Lane
subLocations.lore: A short shady lane with dark alleys that offered hiding spots for ne'er-do-well and an access point to the [[Baldur's Gate/Sewers|sewers]].

subLocations.name: Market Street
subLocations.lore: The street with a butcher shop, rumored to serve monster meat in [[1477 DR]].

subLocations.name: The Western Wet
subLocations.lore: The road that ran alongside the docks from the [[Seatower of Balduran]] to the [[Water Queen's House]].

subLocations.name: The Eastern Wet
subLocations.lore: The street that ran alongside the docks and hugged the harbors from the drydocks on the northern edge of the [[Gray Harbor]] and ended at [[Waendel's Wharf]].

subLocations.name: Waendel's Wharf
subLocations.lore: A wharf of note.

subLocations.name: Stormwynd Dock
subLocations.lore: A dock of note.

subLocations.name: Athcaulyr's Stand
subLocations.lore: A wide and legless dock of note.

subLocations.name: Glaezel's Dock
subLocations.lore: A small dock that had changed many owners and names over the years. It was ran by [[Manthuran Glaezel]] of the wealthy [[Glaezel]] family in the late 14{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Hethkantle's Jetty
subLocations.lore: A dock of note.

subLocations.name: Black Eel Street
subLocations.lore: The road that began at [[Glaezel's Dock]] and moved in a straight line to the west until it ended at the city walls.

subLocations.name: Caundorl Street
subLocations.lore: The road that began at [[Hethkantle's Jetty]] and moved in a straight line to the west until it ended at the city walls.

subLocations.name: Wendserpent Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at [[Black Eel Street]], moved north through the [[Manor Gate]], crossed [[Belltoll Street]], then [[Windspell Street]], passed in front of the [[Black Dragon Gate]], curved along the city walls, passed [[Rose Portal]] shrine, and curved to [[the Wide]], where it ended.

subLocations.name: Wendserpent Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at [[Black Eel Street]], moved north through the [[Manor Gate]], crossed [[Belltoll Street]], then [[Windspell Street]], passed in front of the [[Black Dragon Gate]], curved along the city walls, passed [[Rose Portal]] shrine, and curved to [[the Wide]], where it ended.

subLocations.name: Wendserpent Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at [[Black Eel Street]], moved north through the [[Manor Gate]], crossed [[Belltoll Street]], then [[Windspell Street]], passed in front of the [[Black Dragon Gate]], curved along the city walls, passed [[Rose Portal]] shrine, and curved to [[the Wide]], where it ended.

subLocations.name: Wendserpent Street
subLocations.lore: The street that began at [[Black Eel Street]], moved north through the [[Manor Gate]], crossed [[Belltoll Street]], then [[Windspell Street]], passed in front of the [[Black Dragon Gate]], curved along the city walls, passed [[Rose Portal]] shrine, and curved to [[the Wide]], where it ended.

subLocations.name: Nuthkhal's Way
subLocations.lore: The street that curved, connecting the [[Manycoins House]] with the [[Cliffgate]].

subLocations.name: Nuthkhal's Way
subLocations.lore: The street that curved, connecting the [[Manycoins House]] with the [[Cliffgate]].

subLocations.name: Manyspears Lane
subLocations.lore: The long lane that began at the [[Counting House]], passed the [[Baldur's Gate (gate)|Baldur's Gate]] and encircled [[The Wide]].

subLocations.name: Manyspears Lane
subLocations.lore: The long lane that began at the [[Counting House]], passed the [[Baldur's Gate (gate)|Baldur's Gate]] and encircled [[The Wide]].

subLocations.name: Manyspears Lane
subLocations.lore: The long lane that began at the [[Counting House]], passed the [[Baldur's Gate (gate)|Baldur's Gate]] and encircled [[The Wide]].

subLocations.name: Three Spires
subLocations.lore: One of three major moots in [[Baldur's Gate]] – the intersection of [[Hauth Lane]], [[Wendserpent Street]], and [[Blackraven Lane]].

subLocations.name: Hauth Lane
subLocations.lore: A short street that moved roughly north to south across the [[Three Spires]] intersection.

subLocations.name: Blackraven Lane
subLocations.lore: A short street that moved roughly east to west across the [[Three Spires]] intersection, from the [[Sashenstar]] family estate to [[Chalsendace Street]].

subLocations.name: Chalsendace Street
subLocations.lore: A street of wealth mansions; it stretched from the city walls to [[Stormcanter Street]] by the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]].

subLocations.name: Stormcanter Street
subLocations.lore: A short street on the southern end of [[Chalsendace Street]].

subLocations.name: Fox Bottom
subLocations.lore: One of three major moots in [[Baldur's Gate]]; it was located two city blocks south of [[Manycoins House]] along the [[Stormshore Street]] (formerly known as Long Lane) in a slummy area of run-down rooming-houses.

subLocations.name: Lathdell
subLocations.lore: The small open plaza, or strake, in front of the [[Shrine of the Suffering]].

subLocations.name: Hulkael Street
subLocations.lore: The street that once ran to and past the [[Manycoins House]], later, just stretched between the [[Lathdell]] plaza and [[Murl's Rest]] where the [[Sorcerous Sundries]] store was located.

subLocations.name: Murl's Rest
subLocations.lore: The triangular plaza, or strake, in front of [[Sorcerous Sundries]].

subLocations.name: Lionsmoot
subLocations.lore: One of three major moots in [[Baldur's Gate]], named after [[The House of the Lion]] [[festhall]] located on its eastern angle.

subLocations.name: The House of the Lion
subLocations.lore: An opulent festhall that counted "blades" and "lacethroats"  – youths of money and means, among its patrons.

subLocations.name: Drakon Tavern
subLocations.lore: A relatively small inn and tavern located next door to the [[Gist]] family estate with a small park plaza at the building's back.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Keexie Tavern
subLocations.lore: A simple tavern and inn that served as a front for [[Baldur's Gate]]'s thieves guild in the 14{{th}} century [[DR]], located across the plaza from [[Sorcerous Sundries]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Lucky Aello's Discount Store
subLocations.lore: A store that sold heavily marked-down goods that ranged from [[potion]]s of reliable quality to ''[[curse]]d'' [[weapon]]s and [[scroll]]s of magic protection.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Maltz's Weapon Shop
subLocations.lore: A merchant who dealt in mandate weapons, ran by [[Maltz]] in the 14{{th}} century [[DR]], located just to the northwest of the [[Elfsong Tavern]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Well-Adjusted Al's General Store
subLocations.lore: The general store located to the west of the [[Low Lantern]]; it traded in mundane goods and [[weapon]]s and run by eccentric [[Well-Adjusted Al]] in the 14{{th}} century [[DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Misty Court
subLocations.lore: A street of note where the open-air stonemason's workshop, [[Alabaster Stonecrafts]], could be found.

subLocations.name: Alabaster Stonecrafts
subLocations.lore: An open-air stonemason's workshop run by twin [[dwarf|dwarven]] siblings in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Trident Lane
subLocations.lore: An area in the [[Seatower]] that housed many weapon smiths who serviced the [[Flaming Fist]]. One such shop was run by an automaton in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Saint Sollars Way
subLocations.lore: The street of note on which stood the home ot Mrs. [[Leventide]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Old Town Avenue
subLocations.lore: A street in the [[Lower City]] known for its expensive apartments and lodgings.

subLocations.name: Long Lane
subLocations.lore: A short street that crossed [[Stormshore Street]] at the moot known as [[Fox Bottom]].

subLocations.name: Statue of Balduran
subLocations.lore: A monolithic statue of [[Balduran]], looming over the ships entering the [[Gray Harbor]].

subLocations.name: Stormshore Tabernacle
subLocations.lore: A non-denominational shrine on [[Stormshore Street]].

subLocations.name: Rivington General
subLocations.lore: A smithy that dealt in [[weapon]]s and [[armor]], run by [[Gyldro Angleiron]] after [[1477 DR]]. Its shop area was a building to the north, with the southern connected structure being the workshop and the proprietor's home.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: The Singing Lute
subLocations.lore: A small tavern and an eatery that offered local brews and a grumpy proprietor.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Nortale's Hostel
subLocations.lore: Cheap temporary lodgings, used to house refugees during the [[Absolute crisis]] of [[1492 DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Bonecloak's Apothecary
subLocations.lore: A [[potion]] brewer's shop run by [[Derryth Bonecloak]] and [[Baelen Bonecloak]] ''circa'' [[1492 DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Highberry Home
subLocations.lore: The manse home of [[Cora Highberry]] and [[Roger Highberry]] ''circa'' [[1492 DR]], and the site of their lavish [[wine]] festivals.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Bloomridge Park
subLocations.lore: A small public park nestled at the [[Old Wall (Baldur's Gate)|Old Wall]], east of the [[Manor Gate]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: The Glitter Gala
subLocations.lore: A shop that traded in [[gemstone]]s and jewelry from [[Amn]], [[Cormyr]], and [[Damara]] and shared the building with [[Chromatic Scale]] musical instrument shop.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Chromatic Scale
subLocations.lore: A shop that dealt in quality musical instruments, run by [[Thomas C. Quirkilious]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Sornbanner Street
subLocations.lore: The street that joined [[Belltoll Street]] at a moot in the west and [[Wendserpent Street]] at another moot to the east.

subLocations.name: Facemaker's Boutique
subLocations.lore: An upscale clothier, barber, makeup artist, stylist, and disguises shop.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Sharess' Caress
subLocations.lore: A 15{{th}} century [[DR]] [[festhall]] where one could find consorts, musicians, drinks, food, lodgings, and more thematic coinlassess who catered to specific tastes.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Crimson Draughts
subLocations.lore: [[Araj Oblodra]]'s [[alchemist]] shop located on [[Stormshore Street]] across from [[Beehive Goods and Wares]] general store in the late 15{{th}} century DR.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Beehive Goods and Wares
subLocations.lore: A general store run by [[Oliver Tefoco]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]] and offered food, [[potion]]s, [[wine]]s, and some general miscellany.{{approx}}

subLocations.name: Fauragates
subLocations.lore: The mansion home of the reclusive moneylender Lord [[Erevvus Qwulthurr]] and his consort, magical [[tattoo]]ist, [[Valanthia Harvonth]] in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].

subLocations.name: Sword Coast Couriers
subLocations.lore: A courier, shipping, and postal agency that operated in the environs and within the city of [[Baldur's Gate]], located in the [[Rivington]] neighborhood in the late 15{{th}} century [[DR]].
